clue.text: Restaurant whose products are delivered with the papers?

definitions.text: Restaurant whose products are delivered with the papers?

parts.words: Restaurant whose products are delivered with the papers
parts.note: a takeaway whose fried food traditionally came wrapped in old newspaper, as if the meal arrived with the morning papers

explanation.surface: A puzzling eatery whose goods turn up alongside the newspaper delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, fried fish and chips were traditionally wrapped in sheets of old newspaper, so 'delivered with the papers' is literally true of the shop's food.
explanation.definitionFit: A takeaway selling battered cod and fried potatoes is a restaurant of a kind, and its wares came wrapped in newsprint.

clue.text: If upset, churchman will try to catch one out

definitions.text: will try to catch one out
definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for a cricketer whose job is catching batsmen out

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the short word if is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: an elder is an office-holder in a Presbyterian church

explanation.surface: A clergyman, if annoyed, will try to trip somebody up.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a fielder tries to catch the ball so that the batsman is out; 'catch one out' sounds like trickery in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the fielding side's players try to take catches that dismiss a batsman.

clue.text: Used to plough a lot

definitions.meaning: the ploughshare is the blade of a plough that cuts the furrow
a portion or allotted part, one's lot

explanation.definitionFit: A ploughshare is the cutting blade of a plough, and a portion allotted to someone is their part of the whole.

clue.text: English remittal order to give information to high-ups!

definitions.note: describes an instrument's purpose, standing for the instrument that gives height readings to pilots

indicators.note: order as a verb asks for these letters to be put into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An English money-transfer instruction meant to brief senior people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges E plus REMITTAL. The 'high-ups' are not bosses but people flying high: aircrew reading their height.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft instrument tells pilots their height above ground or sea level.

clue.text: They try to make us fit to be academics

definitions.text: They try to make us fit
definitions.meaning: physicians try to restore patients to health
holders of the highest university degree, PhDs

explanation.surface: Those who try to get us in shape to become scholars.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicians treat patients to restore health, and scholars with a PhD hold the title too.

clue.text: Poor player has a way with the Queen, pet!

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting actor
ST is short for street, a way
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: An inept actor walks out with royalty and an animal companion.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the Latin Elizabeth Regina, used in crosswords for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rodent commonly kept by children as a household animal.

clue.text: Shaved father Lenin, for instance

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
Lenin was a communist, and a communist is called a Red

explanation.surface: Dad trimmed his beard to look like the Soviet leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim thin layers off something is to cut it down, as a razor does.

clue.text: Leader longs for difficult problems to solve

parts.note: a head is a leader, as of a school
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A boss yearns for tricky puzzles to crack.
explanation.definitionFit: Troublesome matters that cause worry are figuratively pains in the head.

clue.text: A biped with lion's head turns into a horse

indicators.note: turns into signals that these letters change shape into something new

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: head of lion's means only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A two-legged creature with a lion's head is transformed into a steed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns into' rearranges ABIPED plus L, the first letter of 'lion's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied horse has irregular patches of black and white.

clue.text: Stops clothes falling off stretcher

definitions.meaning: the stretchy band in a waistband holds garments up

explanation.definitionFit: Stretchy cord in waistbands keeps trousers up and is itself a material that stretches.

clue.text: Push back a lot of soccer fans in Kent

definitions.note: a phrase for somewhere located in Kent, standing for a town there

indicators.note: back says the word for push is written in reverse order

parts.note: to ram is to push hard
the gate is the attendance at a football match

explanation.surface: Shoving back a big football crowd in a southern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; Margate is one of its seaside towns.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside resort on the north Kent coast is a place located within that county.

clue.text: Imagine a ship bringing a per, feet lover!

parts.note: to dream is to imagine
a boat is a vessel

explanation.surface: Picture a vessel carrying an ideal romantic partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an extremely attractive person, an ideal partner.

clue.text: Desperate chap takes one in a princess

indicators.note: takes ... in means the name swallows the numeral inside it

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the strongman of the British comic The Dandy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A frantic man welcomes a royal lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a famous character from the British children's comic The Dandy; 'takes one in' puts I inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Diana, wife of Prince Charles, was the best-known royal of that title.

clue.text: Turns out toaster

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: The bread-browning appliance flips over.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning round on an axis is turning.

clue.text: Might one say, grisly plaything for a child?

definitions.text: Might one say, grisly plaything for a child?

parts.words: Might one say, grisly plaything for a child
parts.note: grisly sounds like grizzly, a kind of bear, so a cuddly toy bear is jokingly a grizzly plaything

explanation.surface: A gruesome toy for a youngster, as some might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grisly' (gruesome) is a sound-alike of 'grizzly', a North American bear, so the toy is a soft bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed toy bear is a favourite cuddly plaything for children.

clue.text: Got there, and delivered a sermon to people being beheaded

indicators.note: being beheaded means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: preached, as a minister does to a congregation

explanation.surface: Arrived, then sermonised to a crowd facing execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being beheaded' drops the first letter, P, from PREACHED.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive at a destination is to get there.

clue.text: Love to ordain a doctor

indicators.note: doctor as a verb means tamper with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fond of ordaining a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep devotion or worship is a form of love.

clue.text: Stands around undressed on Don's departure

indicators.note: around indicates the letters are moved about into a new arrangement
departure tells us the letters of Don's go out of the mix

explanation.surface: A naked man lingers about after a university lecturer has left.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle UNDRESSEDON and remove D, O, N, S ('Don's departure'): the letters left rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear or tolerate something is to put up with it.

clue.text: Shows up and sets light to film!

definitions.meaning: lets light onto photographic film, taking pictures

explanation.definitionFit: Unmasking reveals someone, and a camera admits light to film to take a shot.

clue.text: Fastens notices round a dog

indicators.note: round says the first word goes around the second

parts.note: sees means notices
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Pins up posters around a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something firm and safe is fixing it in place.

clue.text: Happens to describe state of fields after a good summer?

definitions.text: describe state of fields after a good summer?
definitions.meaning: fields where harvests have grown up well

explanation.definitionFit: Something that arises without warning occurs; and in a good summer the harvest has grown up.

clue.text: Diverting little military chief to main road to small U.S. state

parts.note: CO, commanding officer, is the short form of a military chief
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
Cal is a short form of California

explanation.surface: A minor army boss goes along a highway to a little American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's first major motorway; in crosswords the 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amusing and funny diverts or entertains.

clue.text: One influenced by the stars associated with scales? Yes and no!

definitions.text: One influenced by the stars associated with scales? Yes and no!

parts.words: One influenced by the stars associated with scales? Yes and no
parts.note: a person born under the sign of the Fishes, which have scales, yet not the zodiac sign of the Scales, Libra

explanation.surface: Is a person ruled by the horoscope of the Scales? Both true and false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scales' first suggests Libra, the Scales; the sign meant is the Fishes, creatures with scales, so it is yes and no.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born under the zodiac sign of the Fishes is astrologically governed by the stars.

clue.text: One who gets money from tax system — a quarter

parts.note: PAYE, Pay As You Earn, is the British system of deducting income tax from wages
E, east, is one of the four compass points or quarters

explanation.surface: Someone paid through the income tax scheme gets a fourth share.
explanation.walkthrough: PAYE is the UK's pay-as-you-earn scheme for collecting income tax from wages.
explanation.definitionFit: The person a cheque or payment is made out to receives the cash.

clue.text: Got down from the table?…

parts.note: food swallowed from the dinner table, not a child leaving it

explanation.definitionFit: Food consumed at a meal has been swallowed.

clue.text: They show us the way to identify various points

definitions.text: They show us the way to identify various points

parts.words: They show us the way to identify various points
parts.note: navigation instruments that find north, south and the other directions

explanation.surface: Guides who lead us so we can pinpoint different spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic navigation instruments indicate the cardinal points and direction of travel.

clue.text: …& cook something coming off the boil

definitions.meaning: the vapour rising from boiling water

explanation.definitionFit: Cooking food in vapour is one method, and vapour rises from boiling water.

clue.text: Jersey's Gradgrind!

definitions.meaning: Gradgrind, in Dickens's Hard Times, is a harsh employer who overworks people

explanation.walkthrough: Gradgrind is the hard-hearted mill-town figure in Dickens's novel Hard Times, a byword for exploiting workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted pullover is a jersey, and an exploitative boss who overworks staff is one.

clue.text: One of a billion people in the laundry business

definitions.text: One of a billion people in the laundry business

parts.words: One of a billion people in the laundry business
parts.note: a member of the world's most populous nation, long associated with running laundries in Western cities

explanation.surface: A laundry worker from a country of over a billion inhabitants.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation with over a billion people is China, and its people are traditionally linked with laundries abroad.

clue.text: Mighty dumb chap, seemingly, but attractive to many women

definitions.note: an adjective phrase standing for the taciturn tough-guy type said to appeal to women

parts.note: strong means mighty
silent means not speaking, dumb
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A powerful, silent fellow who seems stupid but still charms women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumb' seems to mean stupid, but here it means not speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The taciturn tough-guy type is a stock romantic hero supposed to appeal to women.
